claims.notes: SCOPE DECISION for this whole document (logged here per rule 5, applies to the file as a whole): docs/methodology/transparency/cc-session-archiving-addendum.md is a design/specification draft ('Version: 1.0-draft-addendum-1', 2026-01-08) proposing a session-archiving schema, not a results document. The great majority of its numbers are either (a) illustrative example values inside JSON/YAML schema mockups (e.g. 'count': 89 thinking blocks, total_bytes: 4567890, total_duration_hours: 28.5 in the CATALOG.json example, model version strings) that are not asserted as fact about the study (the Task section's core test) — they illustrate a proposed field's shape, not a measured value — or (b) generic, non-project-specific heuristic tables (A2.2 tool-output-size ranges 'based on typical CC usage patterns', the Light/Medium/Heavy/Intensive session-type table, the A5.7 Adoption Friction Analysis workflow-timing table, the gzip '5-10x reduction' figure, the '<2 minutes' community-adoption target) describing the proposed tool in general, not this project specifically. None of these were extracted. The two claims in this file (this one and the 100-500 MB claim at line 124) are the sole places the document makes a numeric assertion explicitly named to 'the study' (the parenthetical 'e.g., VLM burial mound project' at line 122, immediately preceding this bullet). Even so, this is a forward-looking design-time projection (dated 2026-01-08, early in the project) for a session-archiving campaign; the repo contains no archive/cc-sessions/ directory at extraction time (confirmed: git ls-files and a filesystem check both return nothing), so no committed artefact could be identified as an anchor — left anchor-unknown for all three values.
